restitution.form: e = 0.510 - 0.0375 v + 0.000903 v^2 (v the impact speed in m/s, up to 20 m/s); 0.120 beyond
restitution.source: Penner (2002), 'The run of a golf ball', Can. J. Phys. 80:931-940, doi:10.1139/p02-035, fitted to Haake's (1989) turf data

contact_angle_degrees.source: Penner (2002), as above: the compliant turf's effective inclination for impact speed v and impact angle theta

green_bounce.behaviour: balls typically lift off slipping after their spin reverses: wedges check, drivers release

measurements.source: Biber, Jones, Champneys, Green & Szalai (2023), 'Measurements and linearized models for golf ball bounce on a green', Sports Engineering 26:50, doi:10.1007/s12283-023-00442-4: over 1000 bounces, restitution, friction and Penner's contact angle fitted to them

rolling_sphere_on_slope.source: a solid sphere rolling without slipping (I = 2/5 m r^2)

resistance.form: deceleration = (5/7) rho_r g, rho_r = (k / s)(1 + 0.0065 v^2) for a stimp reading s in feet; Penner's shape, with k = 0.7756 so that a ball rolling off the stimpmeter at 1.83 m/s rolls s feet (Penner's own 0.7028 rolls it 10% further)
resistance.source: Penner (2002), 'The physics of putting', Can. J. Phys. 80:83-96; the stimpmeter's definition

stimpmeter.source: USGA Stimpmeter: the ball leaves the bar at about 6 ft/s; its roll in feet is the green's speed

holding_slope_degrees_at_stimp_10.note: a ball rests where (5/7) g sin(theta) is below its rolling resistance

wetness.note: wet greens roll slower (lower stimp) and softer; fairway and rough have stimp-equivalent resistance from turf research (USGA Green Section, STRI); no single primary number recorded here
